about.title: About Debt Payoff Calculator
about.description: The Debt Payoff Calculator helps you compare debt repayment strategies, payoff timelines, and total interest across multiple balances. It analyzes current debts and lets you review approaches such as debt snowball and debt avalanche using your entered payment assumptions. Use it as a planning reference when organizing repayment scenarios.

howTo.title: How to Use the Debt Payoff Calculator

steps.description: Select between debt snowball (lowest balance first) or debt avalanche (highest interest first).

steps.description: Analyze estimated payoff dates and total interest differences across strategies.

faq.q: What's the difference between debt snowball and debt avalanche?
faq.a: Debt snowball focuses on paying off the smallest balance first, while debt avalanche targets the highest interest rate first. Avalanche often reduces interest more quickly, while snowball may feel easier to follow for some people.

faq.q: How much extra should I pay toward my debts?
faq.a: The amount depends on your budget, other obligations, and emergency savings needs. Even modest extra payments may change the payoff timeline and total interest, so use the calculator to compare scenarios.

faq.q: Should I pay off debt or save money first?
faq.a: This depends on your cash flow stability, emergency savings, debt costs, and financial priorities. Many people balance a basic cash reserve with debt repayment, but the right approach varies by situation.

faq.q: Is debt consolidation a good option?
faq.a: Debt consolidation may be useful if it changes your rate, fees, repayment term, or payment structure in a way that fits your plan. Compare total costs and account terms carefully before deciding.
